correctness.rationale: The repaired RESULT.md counts all cliques, including the empty set, on nonzero elements. From multiplication, commutation within a diagonal index is group commutation and across distinct diagonal indices holds automatically. An off-diagonal element is incompatible with any diagonal at its endpoints. Two off-diagonals commute iff both products vanish: when both are nonzero they lie in different diagonal positions. Hence occupied source and target supports of chosen off-diagonals are disjoint and uniquely determined by the clique. For fixed occupied supports of sizes s,t, choosing arbitrarily from the labeled pairs on allowed i,j sub-supports gives (1+z)^(mij); inclusion–exclusion enforces that each support index occurs. Unused indices give independent factors P_G, the empty-off-diagonal case gives P_G^n, and the multinomial counts each ordered support partition once. Zero is optional and multiplies by 1+z. The original maximal classification and its derived formulas are also correct: saturation fills the rectangle and maximal abelian group choices on unused indices; threshold size maximization follows from discrete convexity of (n−x)a+m floor(x²/4), attained at x=0 or n. Their removal is for coverage, not error. Independent finite replay: python3 /workspace/branches/56f9329d-edcb-444d-8077-3debe5330f94/independent_brandt_check.py C1 and the same command with S3. Direct multiplication and clique enumeration matched all coefficients for B_2(C_1) and B_2(S_3), including the empty term (see independent_brandt_check.out). At n=2 the support term is exactly 2[(1+z)^m−1]. The repaired all-order proof is not inferred from the finite tests. The unchanged frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Repaired claim only: the whole clique polynomial is a natural graph invariant and conveys partial configurations of every size, not just maximal ones. It reduces a graph on n²|G| vertices to explicit polynomial operations using the group-level polynomial and order, without listing intersections of maximal families. The exact uniform transform for all index sizes and arbitrary finite structure groups is useful apart from the covered extremal and maximal statements.
